solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Location reference after chapter and verse (8)

blocks.note: an ode is a poem, a piece of verse

annotation.surface: A scholar citing a Bible passage by chapter and verse.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a scripture citation, but 'after' is not a position word here: it gives POST, the Latin prefix, which then leads the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A postcode is the code on an address that pins down a location.

entries.clue: Ignore ticket times (4,2)

blocks.note: a pass is a ticket for entry or travel

annotation.surface: An instruction to overlook a parking ticket's printed times.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Times' is the multiplication sign: three by four is three times four.
annotation.definitionFit: To pass by something is to let it go unnoticed, to ignore it.

entries.clue: Seat maker left stuffing more down (7)

indicators.note: L is stuffed into the other word, filling it

blocks.note: down = sad, so more down = sadder; it takes the L inside

annotation.surface: An upholsterer filling a cushion with extra down feathers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' and 'down' conjure feather cushions; here down means gloomy. The seat is a saddle, and a saddler makes it.
annotation.definitionFit: A saddler makes saddles, the seats a rider sits on.

entries.clue: Potholer cut by scrap iron in desperation to get out (5,5)

indicators.note: the potholer is cut open and the other pieces set in the gap

blocks.note: a potholer explores caves: a caver; it is split C-A...VER around the rest
to bin something is to scrap it
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

annotation.surface: A cave explorer, hemmed in by scrap metal, desperate to escape.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface and the definition share a mood: a trapped potholer really would feel desperation to get out.
annotation.definitionFit: Cabin fever is the restless irritability of being cooped up too long, a craving to get out.

entries.clue: Dog coming from Sedan died in Montpellier (6,7)

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the letters of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A dog that set out from Sedan and died in the south of France.
annotation.walkthrough: Two French towns make a travel tale. The Dandie Dinmont is a Scottish terrier, named after a farmer in a Walter Scott novel.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Dandie Dinmont is a Scottish terrier breed, named after a farmer in Walter Scott's Guy Mannering.

entries.clue: The king has false teeth (6)

blocks.note: the Crown stands for the monarch

annotation.surface: Gossip that the monarch wears dentures.
annotation.walkthrough: The king also wears crowns, which makes the surface slyly true. A dental crown is a cap fitted over a tooth.
annotation.definitionFit: Crowns are artificial caps fitted over damaged teeth.

entries.clue: Republican likely winner in contest (4)

blocks.note: an ace is a champion, someone expected to win

annotation.surface: A Republican tipped to win an election.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface makes 'contest' look like an election, and a race it is, just not the one the wordplay builds.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: any race, on foot or at the polls, pits rivals against each other.

entries.clue: All the way to the summit sounded flatter on paper (5,2)

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, and the answer is spelt differently

blocks.clueFragment: All the way to the summit
blocks.note: right up = all the way up to the top

annotation.surface: A climber's ascent that sounded smoother when written up afterwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like level ground beside the summit, but it is the verb: to write up is to praise in print.
annotation.definitionFit: To write someone up is to praise them in a written report or review.

entries.clue: Guard deployed to trouble spot, perhaps, felt exposed (8)

indicators.note: the word loses its outer layer, leaving the inside bare

blocks.note: troops deployed to a trouble spot are sent in

annotation.surface: A soldier posted to a war zone who felt vulnerable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' here means stripped, not vulnerable. 'Perhaps' flags that a trouble spot is just one place troops are sent in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sentinel is the sentry posted to keep watch.

entries.clue: Spades suffice for flipping turf (3)

indicators.note: DO is flipped over, reading backwards

blocks.note: that will do = that will suffice

annotation.surface: Spades are enough to turn over the turf in a garden.
annotation.walkthrough: The gardening surface makes 'flipping' sound like turning soil; it reverses DO.
annotation.definitionFit: Sod is a piece of turf, grass with its soil.

entries.clue: A blessing turning in, to nice bed (11)

indicators.note: the letters turn, changing their order

annotation.surface: Someone thankful to be turning in to a comfortable bed at last.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning in' reads as going to bed, but the comma splits it: 'turning' is the instruction, and 'in' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A benediction is a blessing, especially at the end of a service.

entries.clue: Photograph duke and fit Tory peer jogging (13)

indicators.note: the letters are jogged, knocked into a new order

blocks.note: ague is a fever with fits of shivering

annotation.surface: A snapshot of an aristocrat and a sporty Conservative lord out running.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective for a jogger; it is a noun, a bout of fever. A daguerreotype is the early photograph made on a silvered plate.
annotation.definitionFit: A daguerreotype is an early type of photograph, fixed on a metal plate.

entries.clue: Plebeian at heart desires property (10)

indicators.note: only the heart, the centre of the word, is taken

blocks.note: the middle two letters of pleBEian

annotation.surface: A commoner who, deep down, wants to own things.
annotation.walkthrough: An eight-letter word has two letters at its heart, so both B and E are taken.
annotation.definitionFit: Your belongings are the things you own, your property.

entries.clue: Undiscovered monster still what gets inspector going (4)

indicators.note: points to the letter that the next phrase describes
the start of a word is what gets it going

blocks.note: yet = still, as in not yet done

annotation.surface: A monster that remains hidden, prompting an inspector to begin a search.
annotation.walkthrough: The detective surface has the inspector starting a hunt; what actually gets him going is his own first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is a Himalayan monster no one has ever found.

entries.clue: First see rider’s speed then hide (10)

blocks.note: a canter is a horse's moderate pace
to bury something is to hide it

annotation.surface: A horse rider told to look first, then gallop off and hide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb: a see is a bishop's seat, and Canterbury is the senior see of the Church of England.
annotation.definitionFit: Canterbury, the Archbishop's seat, ranks first among English dioceses.

entries.clue: Associate day with purpose (6)

blocks.note: an end is an aim, a purpose

annotation.surface: Someone linking a particular day with a sense of purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Associate' reads as a verb; the answer takes it as a noun, a companion.
annotation.definitionFit: Associate taken as a noun, a companion you keep company with, is a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Paper plane out of an illustration (7)

indicators.note: AN is taken out of the word before it

annotation.surface: A paper plane folded from an old drawing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paper plane' reads as one toy; split it, and paper is an exam while plane is fodder for the deletion.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a case offered to show how a rule works illustrates it.

entries.clue: Account empty following one sharp fall (4,4)

indicators.note: 'following' means coming after, so the word for empty is placed after the one

blocks.note: to drain a thing is to empty it

annotation.surface: A bank account emptied after a steep drop in shares.
annotation.walkthrough: The finance surface makes 'sharp fall' a crash in value; it is rain that is acidic, sharp to taste.
annotation.definitionFit: Acid rain is rainfall made sharply acidic by pollution.

entries.clue: Thus returning seabird in reservoir (7)

indicators.note: SIC comes back, reading right to left

blocks.note: sic is Latin for thus, as printed after a quoted error

annotation.surface: A seabird coming back to settle on a reservoir.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it wants a container, but the bird sits after CIS, not inside anything.
annotation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank that stores water, a small reservoir.

entries.clue: Gibbon lives up a tropical fruit tree, mostly (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads upwards, reversed
most of the word is kept, dropping the last letter

annotation.surface: An ape living high in a tropical fruit tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The jungle surface fits the answer exactly. The siamang is a large black gibbon of Malaysia and Sumatra.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this black ape of Sumatra and Malaysia is the largest species of gibbon.

entries.clue: Beastly drink got stirred in trough (6)

indicators.note: the letters of GOT are stirred into a new order
the mixed letters go inside the trough

blocks.note: a rut is a groove or trough; it holds the rest

annotation.surface: Some awful liquor that was stirred into an animal trough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' and 'trough' paint a farmyard; beastly is just the definition's adjective, meaning foul.
annotation.definitionFit: Rotgut is cheap, harsh alcohol, a beastly drink.

entries.clue: Suffer in Berlin and consequently in Rome (7)

blocks.note: 'and' put into German, as spoken in Berlin

annotation.surface: A traveller suffering in Germany and then again in Italy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places the suffering in Berlin, but 'in Berlin' tells you to put the next word into German, and 'in Rome' the word before it into Latin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to go through hardship is to suffer it.

entries.clue: Daughter given pasta first did shut up (6)

indicators.note: the pasta comes before the daughter

annotation.surface: A child who went quiet once served pasta.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as falling silent; it means shut in, as sheep are penned.
annotation.definitionFit: To pen animals is to shut them up in an enclosure; penned is its past tense.

entries.clue: For men, women’s clothes seem uninteresting (4)

blocks.note: female dress when a man wears it, as on stage
to be tedious, so that time seems to crawl

annotation.surface: A man finding women's fashion rather boring.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'men' makes the first half a definition: clothes of women, when a man wears them.
annotation.definitionFit: Drag is women's dress worn by men; time drags when things are dull.

entries.clue: Spend time inside bank after door locks quietly (2,8)

indicators.note: the door locks P inside itself
RIDGE comes after the door

blocks.note: as printed; it is split DO...OR around P
a bank is a raised ridge of earth

annotation.surface: Staying indoors by a bank once the door is quietly locked.
annotation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, so to do porridge is to serve time. The locked door suits both readings.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from British prison slang, where being inside means locked up in jail.

entries.clue: Keen learner pulls over (4)

indicators.note: the word is turned over, reading backwards

annotation.surface: A driver-in-training who pulls over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pulls over' reads as stopping a car; the two words split into fodder and instruction. A swot is British slang for a studious pupil.
annotation.definitionFit: A swot is someone who studies hard, a keen learner.

entries.clue: On one’s holiday too? How fantastic (4,4,3)

blocks.note: read literally: away, in your company

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker delighted to hear a friend is coming too.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' seems to cheer; it means unbelievable, and 'away with you!' is how you tell someone they're spinning a tall tale.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Away with you!' dismisses a story as too fantastic to believe.

entries.clue: A point, going with twenty-two’s sport (3)

definitions.text: A point, going with twenty-two’s sport

indicators.note: N goes alongside the sport

blocks.note: RU = rugby union, whose pitch has a line called the twenty-two
N = north, a point of the compass

annotation.surface: A game noted as the sport played by a team of twenty-two.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is the definition too: cricket is played on a pitch twenty-two yards long, and a run is its single point.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes a run: the unit of score in cricket, the game of the twenty-two-yard pitch.

entries.clue: Cancel opening at 45 degrees? (6)

blocks.note: north-east is a bearing of 45 degrees
a gate is an opening in a fence

annotation.surface: A door cut on the slant, sending an order to call it off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cancel opening' reads as calling off a launch. The question mark admits a gate facing north-east is a playful picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to cancel something out is to nullify its effect.

entries.clue: Dry veg cook peeled stews OK (4,4)

indicators.note: the word loses its skin, its outer letters
the letters are stewed, mixed up

annotation.surface: A kitchen verdict that stews made from dried vegetables are acceptable.
annotation.walkthrough: A cook peeling veg is the picture, but 'peeled' strips the cook himself down to OO.
annotation.definitionFit: Very good is a formal way of saying OK, agreed.
